name: Tuvalu
summary: A light blue ensign with the Union Flag in the canton and nine yellow stars arranged as a map of the country's nine islands. It was briefly replaced in 1995–1997, then restored.
origin: Tuvalu, formerly the Ellice Islands, became independent on 1 October 1978 with this flag.
In 1995 the government removed the Union Flag and adopted a new design with eight stars in a triangle. It was unpopular, and the original was restored in 1997.

symbols.name: Nine stars
symbols.description: Yellow stars arranged like the islands on a map, with north toward the hoist.
symbols.meaning: The nine islands of Tuvalu; the name means 'eight standing together', since one island was originally uninhabited.

facts: Its stars are a map of the islands, rotated so north points to the hoist.
Tuvalu is one of the countries most threatened by sea-level rise.
Its internet domain, .tv, is a major source of government income.
clues: A light blue ensign with the Union Flag and nine yellow stars forming a map.
Its country's name means 'eight standing together'.
It was replaced in 1995 and brought back in 1997.
